Octen AI’s Deep Research appears to be a research feature inside Octen’s broader AI search platform, built to generate sourcebacked research across thousands of web pages and documents rather than only return a short search answer.  Octen presents it as one part of a larger retrieval stack for AI agents that also includes live web search, URL extraction, embeddings, multimodal chat, and grounded generation.[1][2]

 Product scope

On its homepage, Octen describes itself as “search infrastructure for AI” with realtime indexing, low latency, and high reliability, which suggests it is aimed primarily at developers building agents and AI applications rather than only end users doing oneoff searches.  The Deep Research capability is framed as a way to analyze large sets of web pages and documents with explicit source backing.[2][1]

 Technical approach

Octen contrasts ordinary human search with an AIoriented workflow where multiple subqueries run concurrently, a design it presents as better suited to multistep research tasks.  The platform also says it can turn URLs into clean markdown with page classification and intentfocused highlights, which makes retrieved material easier for language models to consume downstream.[2]

 Claimed performance

According to Octen and launch coverage, the company claims roughly 60 to 62 millisecond response times, minutelevel or about fiveminute data freshness, and support for more than 1 million queries per second.  Octen also says its OctenEmbedding8B model led the RTEB leaderboard in January 2026, while its multimodal embedding model led MMEBv2 in May 2026.[3][4][5][2]

 Business context

Octen announced a $10 million seed round in 2026 led by Square Peg with Argor participating, and reporting around the launch said the web search API was in inviteonly beta.  Coverage also describes the company as operating from San Francisco and Singapore under founder Kuan Zou, whose background includes search and AI infrastructure work at Alibaba Cloud and Baidu.[5][6][3]

 How to assess it

If you are evaluating Octen specifically for deepresearch workflows, the clearest pitch in the available material is live, sourcebacked retrieval for agent systems that need many concurrent searches, not just a single chatbot response.  Most of the detailed benchmark and performance information currently available comes from Octen’s own materials or reporting based on its launch announcement, so the practical question is whether it outperforms alternatives on your real workload.[4][5][2]

Would you like a vendorbyvendor comparison of Octen vs Perplexity, Exa, Tavily, and Brave for deepresearch use cases?
